name: Scheduled Tasks
os_min: Windows Vista (XML tasks); legacy .job on XP
location: C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\<TaskName> (XML); registry mirror at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree and \Tasks
purpose: Defines actions executed on a schedule or trigger (logon, event, time); a common legitimate and malicious persistence mechanism.
normal_baseline: Tasks correspond to installed software's update/maintenance routines and OS-native scheduled maintenance.
anomalies: Action node pointing to Temp/AppData with base64-encoded PowerShell arguments
Suspicious repetition interval (e.g. every few minutes)
Task registered without a corresponding Security 4698 event, suggesting log gaps or non-standard creation (e.g. direct XML drop)
parsing_tools: TaskScheduler view + PECmd/Registry Explorer for TaskCache
anti_forensic_notes: TaskCache registry entries can persist under \Tasks\{GUID} even after the XML file is deleted, useful for timeline reconstruction. Event IDs 4698/4699 require Object Access auditing to be enabled, which many environments lack by default.
